nodes.label: Q: Why the Origin packing list bridges Creature Identity to Click-Through Overlay Physics
nodes.norm_label: q: why the origin packing list bridges creature identity to click-through overlay physics
nodes.rationale: The snapshot README's packing list is the bridge node: seven of its eight edges point at identity/chrome items, but one member is a rendering surface, which pulls it out of the identity community. The load-bearing hop is INFERRED, not EXTRACTED - CSS pointer-events in the web-origin snapshot and WS_EX_TRANSPARENT in Haiky solve the same problem at different stack layers with no import, call or citation linking them. The identity half of the port was copied verbatim while the physics half was re-implemented lower down, which is why only an inferred edge joins them.

nodes.label: Q: Which creature physics crossed into main, which stayed in the DOM, and what decided the split
nodes.norm_label: q: which creature physics crossed into main, which stayed in the dom, and what decided the split
nodes.rationale: The whole simulation stayed in the DOM and only what needs OS authority crossed into main. The deciding rule quoted from src/main/overlay.js:169 is that the renderer publishes a fact and main draws the conclusion: simulation stays where it can run at frame rate, arbitration moves where it cannot be dropped, because a hit test that says yes and never says no again leaves every click landing on invisible glass. No extracted edge exists between renderer physics and src/main/ - the link runs entirely through preload.js channel names that the AST cannot follow across contextBridge, and that near-disjointness is itself evidence the seam is clean.

nodes.label: Claude Code Signal Pipeline (sessions.js, bridge.js, hooks.js)
nodes.norm_label: claude code signal pipeline (sessions.js, bridge.js, hooks.js)
nodes.rationale: sessions.js watches ~/.claude/sessions/, bridge.js is the loopback HTTP server the hooks post to, and hooks.js merges a block into ~/.claude/settings.json - together they turn Claude Code activity into the run state the creature reacts to.

nodes.label: Comments Explain Why, Not What
nodes.rationale: Comments in this codebase are load-bearing documentation rather than restatements of the code; contributors must match that register and must not strip them.

nodes.label: The MASCOT.md Promise Is Kept By Not Sending
nodes.norm_label: the mascot.md promise is kept by not sending
nodes.rationale: haiky:talk sends the mood, the run state, the open folders and where the creature is standing - and nothing else. No path, no transcript, no code. The privacy promise in MASCOT.md is kept structurally, by not sending them, rather than by a setting.

nodes.label: Read IPC.md Before Crossing the Preload
nodes.norm_label: read ipc.md before crossing the preload
nodes.rationale: Import graphs cannot see channel names, so the wire between main.js, overlay.js and renderer/mascot.js is invisible to every static tool including this project's own knowledge graph. IPC.md is what makes it visible; a new channel not added there is a channel nothing can find later.

nodes.label: The Renderer Never require()s Anything
nodes.rationale: src/renderer/ holds pose sampling, physics and drawing and never requires anything, because src/main/preload.js is the only boundary - eleven named channels are the entire surface between the page and the main process.

nodes.label: Graphify Query-First Convention
nodes.rationale: For codebase questions run graphify query/path/explain against graphify-out/graph.json first, because they return a scoped subgraph much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep; run graphify update after modifying code to keep the graph current.

nodes.label: Haiky - Electron Creature on a Click-Through Taskbar Overlay
nodes.norm_label: haiky - electron creature on a click-through taskbar overlay
nodes.rationale: The creature lives on a transparent, click-through overlay over the Windows taskbar and reacts to what Claude Code is doing; main.js orchestrates, overlay.js owns the window and the 30Hz hit test, and the renderer is the creature itself.

nodes.label: Tray Icons Drawn From the Creature's Superellipse
nodes.norm_label: tray icons drawn from the creature's superellipse
nodes.rationale: build/make-icon.js draws the tray icons from the same superellipse the creature uses, so the tray and the creature cannot drift apart in shape. Regenerated with npm run icon.

nodes.label: Vendor Snapshot Is Read Only
nodes.rationale: vendor/removed-snapshot/ is a verbatim copy of the app Haiky's creature came from and nothing loads it; the point is that it is unchanged, so its bugs must not be fixed, reformatted or cleaned up. Its .js files under host/ are prose with code excerpts, not runnable JavaScript, and their parse errors are expected.

nodes.label: Never Bump a DOCS version Casually
nodes.norm_label: never bump a docs version casually
nodes.rationale: load() falls back to defaults on a version mismatch, so bumping a version in store.js DOCS discards that document - for the usage document that is the user's whole spend history.
